name: Trade Finance and Transshipment Obfuscation for Proliferation
description: Proliferation procurement uses letters of credit, open-account trade and transshipment hubs to obscure origin, destination and end use of controlled items. Document inconsistencies and unusual routing are the principal observable indicators for trade finance teams.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
FATF, Guidance on Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment and Mitigation (2021)
FATF/Egmont, Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments (2020)

exposure.rationale: LCs, open-account trade and transshipment documentary inconsistencies.

indicators.name: Routing via transshipment hubs unconnected to buyer or seller
indicators.canon: Routing through trade-diversion or transshipment hubs
indicators.desc: Goods or payments route through third-country hubs or ports with no commercial rationale, or hubs known for rerouting.
indicators.ctx: Goods travel through third-country ports with no commercial need and are reloaded or relabelled.
indicators.fp: Hubs are efficient routes for many legitimate exporters.

indicators.name: Letter of credit terms that are unusually flexible or amended repeatedly
indicators.canon: Letter of credit terms that are unusually flexible or amended repeatedly
indicators.desc: Frequent amendments to beneficiary, destination or description, or acceptance of discrepant documents.
indicators.ctx: Frequent amendments to beneficiary, destination or description, or acceptance of discrepant documents.

indicators.name: Goods description vague or generic for high-risk categories
indicators.desc: Trade documents use generic terms or imprecise descriptions or mismatched HS codes where specifics would be expected.
indicators.ctx: Documents use generic terms such as 'machinery' or 'parts' where technical specifics would be expected.

indicators.name: Inconsistent origin and destination across documents
indicators.canon: Trade documents inconsistent with each other
indicators.desc: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.
indicators.ctx: Certificate of origin, invoice and shipping data disagree on country of origin or consignee.

indicators.name: Payments by parties in different jurisdictions with no trade link
indicators.canon: Payments from or for third parties unrelated to the underlying trade
indicators.desc: Payments are made by parties with no apparent link to the underlying transaction, goods or services.
indicators.ctx: Settlement arrives from unrelated entity or country relative to the trade parties.
indicators.fp: Third-party settlement is not unusual in supply chains.

indicators.name: Open-account trade with buyers in high-risk jurisdictions lacking track record
indicators.canon: Open-account trade with buyers in high-risk jurisdictions lacking track record
indicators.desc: New relationships with large unsecured trade flows to or from countries of proliferation concern.
indicators.ctx: New relationships with large unsecured trade flows to or from countries of proliferation concern.

indicators.name: Vessel, voyage or shipper details missing or implausible
indicators.canon: Vessel, voyage or shipper details missing or implausible
indicators.desc: Transport documents lack vessel identifiers or show impossible voyage timing.
indicators.ctx: Transport documents lack vessel identifiers or show impossible voyage timing.
indicators.fp: Booking details can change before departure.

indicators.name: Re-export of controlled items by distributors in transit jurisdictions
indicators.canon: Re-export of controlled items by distributors in transit jurisdictions
indicators.desc: Importer reorders and quickly re-exports technical items to another country.
indicators.ctx: Importer reorders and quickly re-exports technical items to another country.
